 Order

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for setting aside the impugned order dated 22.11.2023 and seeking quashment of FIR No.73/2023, dated 22.02.2013, registered at Police Station: Vishwavidhyalaya, District Rewa and all consequential proceedings subsequent thereto.

2. Facts of the case reveals that the prosecution case is that the complainant lodged a report at Police Station Vishwavidyalaya, District Rewa (M.P.), alleging that her marriage with the petitioner was solemnized on 24.02.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs.
It is alleged that after marriage, the petitioner and his family members subjected her to cruelty and harassment in connection with dowry demands.
It is further alleged that the petitioner took the complainant to Bareilly, where he was employed, and demanded a two-wheeler and a car.
On being informed, the complainant's father allegedly transferred an amount of Rs. 3.25 lakhs through RTGS into the petitioner's bank account.

The prosecution further alleges that the petitioner obtained an ex-parte decree of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9996 2 MCRC-4104-2024 divorce on 12.02.2020, yet continued to cohabit with the complainant and established physical relations with her.
It is alleged that upon her becoming pregnant, the petitioner forcibly caused an abortion.
On 05.03.2021, the petitioner allegedly turned the complainant out of his house, after which she has been residing with her parents.

On the basis of the aforesaid allegations, FIR No. 0/2022 dated 10.02.2022 was registered at Police Station Vishwavidyalaya, District Rewa (M.P.), and subsequently transferred to Police Station Cantt., District Bareilly (U.P.), where FIR No. 63/2022 dated 18.02.2022 was registered for offences under Sections 498-A and 376(2)(n) IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Harish Kumar Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114484534/

sentences.text: FIR No. 73/2023 dated 22.02.2023 was thereafter registered.

After completion of investigation,
the police filed the charge-sheet, and the case was committed to the Court of Sessions.
By order dated 22.11.2023, the learned Trial Court framed charges against the petitioner under Sections 498-A, 376(2)(n), and 312 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
A certified copy of the said order is filed as Annexure A-4.
That, the petitioner submits that he has been falsely implicated and has not committed any offence.

The FIR was lodged after obtaining an ex-parte decree of divorce, solely as an afterthought and to counter matrimonial proceedings, despite the fact that it was the complainant who subjected the petitioner to cruelty.
The ex-parte decree of divorce was subsequently set aside by the learned Family Court by judgment and decree dated 16.12.2023 passed in RCSHM No. 185/2019.
Against the said judgment, the petitioner has also preferred First Appeal No. 25 of 2024 before this Hon'ble Court.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned order dated 22.11.2023 and FIR no.73/2023 are wholly illegal, arbitrary and in violation of the procedure.

The learned Trial Court while framing the charges under section NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9996 3 MCRC-4104-2024 498-A of IPC and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,376(2)(N) and 312 of IPC failed to consider the material fact that the FIR has been lodged with extra ordinary delay of 2 years and further the place of incident as per story narrated in FIR is District Bareli (U.P.) and therefore the Session Court Rewa had no jurisdiction to entertain the said FIR no. 73/2023.
Hence, the impugned order dated the impugned order dated 22.11.2023 and FIR no. 73/2023 is liable to be set aside.

It is submitted that the impugned order dated 22.11.2023 has been passed by the learned Trial Court without considering the material fact that the respondent has narrated the story on the basis of ex-parte judgment.
Further in relation to allegations made in the written statement the respondent has not at all filed any documents.

Because, the learned Court below further failed to see that the respondent has admitted in Divorce case the fact that she is living with her parent's from 10.11.2019,
thus it is clear that no such incident took place with the respondent.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that to decide the controversy between the parties it is necessary in the interest of justice that this Court may call for the record from the Court below for its kind perusal and prays for setting aside the impugned order dated 22.11.2023 and seeking quashment of FIR No.73/2023, registered at Police Station: Vishwavidhyalaya, District Rewa and all consequential proceedings subsequent thereto.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner and has supported the impugned judgement.
It is submitted that the judgement passed by the Court below does not calls for interference and prays for dismissal of this petition.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

At the stage of considering a petition for quashment, this Court is not expected to undertake a detailed appreciation of evidence or assess the probable defence of the petitioner.

The defence raised by the petitioner involves disputed questions of fact, including denial of the allegations and justification of the alleged conduct, which can only be examined after parties lead evidence during trial.
